description:
Problem: .github/workflows/oracle-verdict.yml schedules its retry sweep with cron '23 * * * *' (:16-17). The sweep job (:26-56) runs cli sweep, which lists open develop PRs and dispatches oracle-verdict for each head whose latest retry state is pending and due (_project/scripts/oracle_reviewers/cli.py:814-831, retry.py:125-130), at most 5 per sweep (retry.sweep_max_dispatches). GitHub started 65 scheduled runs from 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-22 (3 to 7 a day), and the 30 from 2026-10-20T04:58Z to 2026-10-25T11:41Z were 2.0 to 6.1 hours apart. A head ends pending when every attempted reviewer is absent (the gateway host is asleep or offline, docs/internal/oracle-review-v2.md:64-68); in the 2026-10-21 investigation of 450 attempts, heads with an absence that later got a verdict waited 0.2 to 8.8 hours.

Limits: a dispatched retry plans as a manual run (cli.py:278-296), so decide_rerun (retry.py:74-104) enforces the per-PR daily budget (6 in 24 hours), the doubling backoff from 60 minutes and the absent-reviewers-only same-head rule, and max_attempts (5) bounds reviewer attempts per run. A retry is recorded only when its run finalizes (retry.py:107-122), so a more frequent sweep cannot exceed these limits. It can, however, re-dispatch a head whose retry is still running: due_for_retry ignores in-flight runs, and dispatched runs share the PR's concurrency group with cancel-in-progress (oracle-verdict.yml:21-23), so the new dispatch cancels the running retry before it records anything. This already happens (runs 39792269422 and 39792259190 were cancelled by 39848282933 and 39848273656, which were cancelled by 39864883915 and 39864877587, dispatched right after scheduled sweep 39864739641). Retry runs took up to 60 minutes (39707090161), and develop received 11 to 53 pushes a day over 2026-10-18 to 10-25.

Outcome: due pending heads are dispatched within a measured bound of becoming due, without depending on GitHub's cron cadence, and no sweep cancels an in-flight retry.

Decision gates:
1. Mechanism (default): add push to develop as a trigger of the sweep job only and keep the cron, matching the oracle-gate sweep. Separate jobs, no shared code, no new workflow. A delayed self-dispatch (holds a runner for the backoff) or a scheduler outside GitHub (for example a timer on the gateway host) needs the owner's approval. Record the choice in context before editing.
2. In-flight guard. The sweep skips any PR with a queued or in-progress oracle-verdict run (Actions runs API, display title pr=N). The sweep job's existing actions: write permission covers reading runs. If the guard needs a new permission or secret, stop and record why.
3. Sweep concurrency. Push and schedule sweeps share one group, separate from every PR group, with cancel-in-progress false, while per-PR groups keep cancel-in-progress. If the group expression (:22-23) cannot express that without changing per-PR grouping, stop and record why.
4. Bound definition. A pending head becomes due at its state's updated_at plus 60 x 2^n minutes, where n is the number of retries in the last 24 hours, while under the daily budget (retry.py:94-101). Measure from that moment to the dispatch.

Item guardrails: no change to decide_rerun, due_for_retry's budget, backoff or attempt rules, .github/oracle-reviewers.yml values, the plan, attempt or post jobs, or the gate dispatch; no new secrets or permissions. oracle-verdict.yml and _project/scripts/oracle_reviewers are soundness paths, so the PR needs the oracle's review.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, after make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. No SKIP or --no-verify, no stand-in approvals, no ruleset edits or bypasses, no raw gh pr merge. Do not change oracle-gate's App binding (integration 5201041), the oracle decision rule, or the native review-thread-resolution requirement. Do not close and reopen, mass-rerun or rebase other pull requests. No explanatory comments or docstrings in code; commits, PR bodies and docs carry no tracker item IDs or session labels; timing uses benchbox.utils.clock.mono_time().
